newsitem.title: USA: Boston Gas rate settlement rejected.
newsitem.headline: Boston Gas rate settlement rejected.

text.p: Eastern Enterprises said Monday Massachusetts regulators had rejected the rate settlement its Boston Gas Co subsidiary reached two weeks ago with the Attorney General's Office, the Department of Energy Resources plus several customer advocacy groups.

Boston Gas was granted a $6.3 million annual rate increase, Eastern said. In May, the natural gas distribution utility sought a $29.9 million rate increase as part of its restructuring proposal. The agreement set a $13 million rise.
The Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities decision was "unsatisfactory," Eastern said in a statement.
It went on to say the department "summarily rejected" the settlement, which was not objected to by any of the 33 parties invloved in the proceeding.

"One positive aspect of the Department's order was the approval of Boston Gas' plan to introduce competition in the commercial and industrial market by providing customers a choice of supplier effective December 1, 1996," said Eastern Chief Executive Officer J. Atwood Ives.

"We are in the process of reviewing the details and the impact of this lengthy decision," continued Ives, "but we have already uncovered a number of major issues which will require departmental clarification. We are also reviewing all of our other options."
Beyond seeking clarification, the utility can apply for a rehearing then appeal to the state courts.
"We were surprised and very disappointed with the Department's unprecedented decision to reject the settlement agreement," Ives said.

"This agreement reflected the views and desires of every customer classification served by Boston Gas. The Department's decision failed to incorporate important elements agreed to by this diverse group of customer representatives, including features which would have provided favorable and stable prices for all energy users.

"The decision also cut in half -- from $13.0 million to $6.3 million -- the additional revenues agreed upon as necessary to maintain a full spectrum of services requested by the customer groups." -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
